title: Karnataka’s weather has been no walk in park - Bangalore Mirror

Karnataka’s weather has been no walk in park
Between January 1 and September 30 this year, Karnataka recorded extreme weather events on 101 of the 273 days. These events claimed 85 lives, damaged 17,006 hectares of crop area and killed 512 animals, according to a report by the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE).
Of the total extreme weather events, Karnataka recorded 42 days of lightning and storms, which claimed 52 lives, while heavy rain, floods and landslides occurred on 63 days, resulting in 32 deaths. The state reported no heatwave days, while coldwave or cold-day conditions were recorded on two days.
The number of days with extreme weather in Karnataka in 2026 was also marginally lower than the 120 days recorded during the corresponding period in 2025. Similarly, the state’s death toll this year, at 85, was lower than the 117 recorded in 2025. Karnataka had 96 days of extreme weather and 86 deaths in 2024, 47 such days and 46 deaths in 2023, and 83 extreme weather event days, resulting in 181 deaths, in 2022.
The figures indicate that while the frequency of extreme weather events in Karnataka has fluctuated over the five-year period, their impact has remained significant. In 2026, nearly 37% of the days between January and September saw extreme weather events in the state.
Across the South Peninsula region, which includes Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and the Union Territories of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and Puducherry, extreme weather events were recorded on 175 of the 273 days in 2026. These events claimed 394 lives and affected around 87,000 hectares of crop area.
Against Karnataka’s 101 days of extreme weather, Kerala recorded 126 such days, leading to 90 deaths. Andhra Pradesh recorded 181 deaths, the highest in the region, despite reporting extreme weather on 54 days.
The report highlights the widespread nature of extreme weather impacts across India. Nationally, the country recorded extreme weather events on 251 of 273 days between January and September 2026. These events claimed at least 3,220 lives, affected 4.25 million hectares of crop area, killed more than 47,244 animals and damaged 128,334 houses.
